properties.description: The capture half of KPPs, and the half a person actually touches. BUILT 2026-07-25 as the kpp-proposal skill (art:kpp-proposal-skill) plus the typed write path it needs. Anthony, 2026-07-25: the user says "the system should be able to perform X"; the agent, acting as the systems-engineering SME the user is not required to be (req:no-se-knowledge), recognises the shape of inviolable intent and asks — that sounds like something that MUST be met, is it? — and the user confirms or declines. WHY THE AGENT MUST NOT DECIDE IT: criticality is a claim about consequence, not about wording. Whether missing a threshold FAILS THE EFFORT depends on mission, contract and money that the graph does not hold and the agent cannot see. An agent that promoted a requirement to KPP on its own would be asserting the user's stake in their own project, which is the same forgery dec:certainty-derived forbids for requirement status — and worse here, because a KPP outranks every ordinary gap and would drag the whole detector's ranking with it. So: the agent PROPOSES, the human DISPOSES, and nothing enters as a KPP without the user's word. WHAT THE AGENT CAN LEGITIMATELY NOTICE, and it is more than intuition. A statement carrying a unit-bearing threshold (500 miles, 3000 pounds, 500 milliseconds) is already shaped like a KPP and may simply be unmodelled — the quantity/limit/direction triple has somewhere to go. Language of necessity ('must', 'shall', 'no less than') against language of preference ('should', 'aims to') is a real signal in acquisition prose. And a requirement whose failure the user has elsewhere described as fatal is a candidate the graph itself can surface. THE QUESTION MUST CARRY THE CONSEQUENCE, not just the label: asking 'is this a KPP?' invites a shrug, whereas asking 'if the system missed this by ten percent, would the effort have failed?' is answerable by someone who has never heard the term — which is the test req:no-se-knowledge sets. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it was the reason this could not be skill-only: add_constraint had no `objective` parameter and its description never mentioned the kpp category, so the only way to record a confirmed KPP over MCP was the generic create_node — which is why the 9 tests of cap:kpp build their KPPs that way. A capture skill would have been pointing the agent at a door that was not there. add_constraint now takes objective and names the category, so what the user confirms is recordable through the typed helper (3 further tests). TWO GUARDS THE SKILL CARRIES that no test can enforce: it must not ask about every requirement (a design where everything is inviolable has no KPPs, and asking becomes noise the user waves through), and on a decline it records a small accepted Decision GOVERNED_BY the node, because the same signals will otherwise make it ask again next session — being asked the same question twice is how someone learns the tool is not listening. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT AUTOMATED: nothing scans the design for KPP candidates on its own. That would be a detector proposing the user's stakes to them, and the ask belongs where the words are still fresh — in the conversation that produced them.
properties.name: Notice when a stated need is really a KPP, and ask
